newsitem.title: USA: Significant issues remain in budget talks - W.House.
newsitem.headline: Significant issues remain in budget talks - W.House.

text.p: The White House took issue with Republican claims Sunday that a deal on budget and tax legislation was imminent, saying there were still significant issues to be worked out.

White House spokesman Joe Lockhart, travelling with President Clinton in Los Angeles, said no high-level meetings took place between the two sides Sunday and suggested optimistic statements made earlier by House Speaker Newt Gingrich were premature.
Gingrich said only minor issues remained to be resolved in budget talks between the White House and Congress, predicting that a final deal was possible on Sunday "if we're lucky."
"I think we have an agreement, it's never done until it's done," Gingrich said as Republicans and administration officials prepared for another round of negotiations in the Capitol.

But Lockhart said Sunday's meetings had involved mostly lower-level officials and significant issues were still unresolved. He said senior administration officials had met among themselves Sunday to discuss the negotiations.
"There are still significant issues to be worked out and until they're worked out, we won't have deal," Lockhart said.
Clinton's reference to the possibility of completing the negotiations as early as Monday came after he described the emerging agreement as a "great opportunity."

"I want us to make this balanced budget agreement tomorrow that I hope 90 percent plus of the Democrats will vote for," Clinton said at a fund-raising dinner for the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee.
"This is a very good budget if we can resolve the remaining problems," the president said. "If we stay in a positive frame of mind. I think we have an excellent chance to get there."

Clinton said the budget deal would provide for the largest increase for child health care since passage of the Medicaid programme for the poor in the mid-1960s and would restore almost all of the cuts in aid to legal immigrants imposed by last year's welfare reform bill.
